q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Data check first: the premise is incorrect — net ROAS rose, and net profit actually improved (loss narrowed) over the window checked. Net ROAS rose from 0.7261x to 0.9424x (+29.8%); net profit moved from a larger loss to a smaller loss (₹-5,51,581 → ₹-62,697), so profit is not declining in the same comparison.

What changed, and why ROAS looks better
- Ad spend fell sharply: P&L ad spend dropped ~19.7% (₹47,393 → ₹38,045, 2026-10-14 → 2026-10-15). Lower spend with only a smaller fall in margin raises ROAS because ROAS = contribution margin ÷ ad spend.
- Contribution margin fell less: contribution margin decreased ~7.7% (₹47,101 → ₹43,452). Because margin fell proportionally less than spend, ROAS increases (ad spend per order fell more than margin per order).
- Traffic and conversions fell but efficiency improved: impressions, clicks and landing-page views all declined (~10–25%), CPC/CPM moved down, and CAC/CPA improved (CAC ₹2,154 → ₹1,522, -29.4%; CPA ₹1,215 → ₹1,028, -15.4%), concentrating the remaining spend into relatively better-performing actions.
- No single upstream cause found: automated diagnosis did not flag an unusual event (budget or returns) that explains this beyond ordinary variation — the ROAS increase is driven arithmetically by a disproportionate fall in spend versus margin.

Worth checking: break ROAS and profit by channel or by the top ads (the diagnosis shows a few ads contributed strongly) to confirm whether efficiency gains are concentrated and whether pulling spend left fixed costs or other P&L lines that could reverse profit later.

Period: 2026-09-16..2026-10-15 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-16
